findings.summary: The new cache-free cleanup claim overlooks gRPC control-item pools that retain payloads and entire transport/stream reference chains after ConnEnd.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/91/reader-contract.md:139-141 says fixed cached bookkeeping is cleared and has no payload references; :207-224 charges scratch only to live leases and permits reuse after ConnEnd/call unwind/empty exactPool ledger. Pinned grpc1.85.0 internal/transport/controlbuf.go:42-87 instead returns itemNode to a process-global sync.Pool without clearing temp.it or temp.next. incomingSettingsHandler (:743-745) leaves incomingSettings.ss intact, so settings arrays from http2_client.go:1341-1365 remain reachable through cached nodes independently of exactPool. More substantially, a cached cleanupStream retains onWrite: http2_client.go:1005-1020 captures t and s, and cleanupStreamHandler (controlbuf.go:883-909) invokes but never clears it. Those closures can retain the old transport, stream, framer and receive-buffer references after ConnEnd. For <=1024 DATA, SliceBuffer.Free is a no-op (mem/buffers.go:306-317), so framer.dataFrame.data can still point to payload backing while the exact-pool ledger is empty. Replacing the response BufferPool and disabling shared transport buffers does not replace itemNodePool. This disproves the claimed cleared-bookkeeping/cleanup component; no whole64MiB overflow is asserted.
findings.fix: Account for pinned internal cached nodes and their full reference chains across completed call/lease-credit reuse, using a concrete process-wide persistent reservation/lifetime rule, or specify a concrete integration change that truly clears those references. Do not assume the exported response pool controls this separate cache or that ConnEnd purges it. Reconcile the retained capacity with D and the same64MiB invariant, and add a future stock-transport fixture covering cached incomingSettings/cleanupStream after success/error and <=1024 DATA, including a subsequent rotated call while prior cached references remain reachable. Preserve the no-internal-import/no-fork statement only for the mechanism actually specified.

findings.summary: Waiting for a Put-empty exactPool ledger permanently strands credits when stock gRPC abandons an unread response root.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/91/reader-contract.md:134-138 retires ledger entries only in Put, and :219-224 requires the ledger to be empty before releasing the call/lease; :373-381 expects error/cancel cleanup and later reuse. A permitted unpadded1025-byte DATA frame whose first5 bytes advertise a gRPC message length R+1 is a concrete counterexample. http_util.go:549-552 allocates it through exactPool.Get; transport.go:353-365 and mem/buffers.go:228-240 consume only the5-byte message header and retain the rest in recvBufferReader.last. rpc_util.go:783-797 then returns ResourceExhausted before reading the body. stream.go:1333-1347 closes the transport stream; http2_client.go:981-1036 merely queues the terminal error/cleanup and closes done, and :1039-1113 closes the connection and reports ConnEnd. None drains r.last or invokes its Free/Put, and there is no root finalizer in mem/buffers.go. Thus call unwind and transport cleanup can finish with an entry which will never receive Put; if the ownership ledger retains its handle, that ledger also keeps the backing alive. Four such completed failures can permanently consume all four leases even after a healthy metadata peer returns. This is a deterministic abandoned-root path, rather than an unknown or still-running cleanup.
findings.fix: Specify an implementable terminal per-call ownership-retirement/drain mechanism for roots abandoned by stock gRPC, with explicit quiescence conditions that exclude late reads/Get/Put and a safe late-Put policy; ordinary last-reference Put remains the normal path. Merely keeping credits forever or assuming every allocated root eventually calls Put does not satisfy the promised recovered normal call. Add the future real-HTTP2 R+1 length/1025-byte single-frame fixture, plus cancellation/codec rejection with queued or partially consumed DATA, and assert actual reclaim/reuse within the stated lifecycle while retaining credit for genuinely active references.
